one_month_reasoning: Window 10/20-11/19/2026 holds: (1) Oct 28 FOMC, hold ~87% (DeFi Rate Kalshi/Polymarket) - little news; (2) Oct 29 Q3 results with first 2027 guidance and the rolled-forward 2027-2031 capital and financing plan. Base rate: XEL has met or beaten guidance 21 years running and roll-forwards usually raise capex; the risk is a bigger equity need. My rate-base build now gives 2027 EPS $4.45 (trimmed for the NSPM 2027-28 freeze proposal and the CPUC historical test year, 8-Ks), slightly under the $4.54 consensus, so a 2027 guide range around $4.40-4.55 is roughly priced; (3) Nov 3 midterms (affordability and data-center politics in MN/CO); (4) the likely Anthropic IPO (Polymarket: November 62%, by Nov 30 65%). On Kilian's liquidity question the nearest base rate is the SpaceX IPO, week of 9 June 2026: the Magnificent Seven all fell, but XEL went 79.04 -> 79.22 and XLU 44.35 -> 44.53 that week (and +1.6% / +2.2% to 6/30; Twelve Data), and the asset-supply channel in the IPO literature (BIS WP 888) hits stocks that co-move with the issuer, while XEL's 2-year beta to SPY is 0.21 (correlation 0.16). So I put no IPO-drain drift into XEL; (5) MPUC Minnesota gas-case decision expected November. The biggest short-run driver remains the 10Y (5.12%, down from 5.31% on 10/5). No momentum or reversal view after the +9% rally off the 9/24 low ($68.72): median ~$76.9, sigma ~5.7% (19% annual vol / 3.5 plus a little for the earnings/plan event), slightly fatter left tail for a plan or equity surprise. Unchanged from round 1 because nothing the supervisor found falls inside the month.

Equity-ratio label (gate check): 54% (2026-27) and 54.5% (2028) are this agent's forward assumption for the authorised operating-company blend (rate-case orders), not the consolidated ~41%; on today's orders the blend is 53.71% (PSCo 54.5%, NSPM 52.5%, SPS 54.7%, NSPW 52.5% on the 2025 mix) and ~53.73% on the 2027 mix, and 54.5% would need ~95% of rate base at PSCo/SPS. Because the 2026 ROE is calibrated to guidance on 54%, only the 2028 step-up matters: at a flat ratio FY2028 EPS is ~$0.05 lower (NTM -$0.04, P/E leg ~-$0.7/sh).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCFF FY2026-30 on revenue $15.6B -> $20.6B, EBIT incl. AFUDC/other income 24.5% -> 31.5%, tax -8% -> +5%, D&A ~20-21% of revenue, capex $13.8/16.1/14.2/10.5B then steady-state $7.7B in FY2030; WACC 6.4%; Gordon 3.5%; net debt at horizon $50.2B; 658M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: 10-K FY2025 income statement 'Total operating revenues 14,669' (XBRL revenue not in the fact pack; read from the filing).

Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_ESTIMATES snapshot saved 2026-10-20T21:17:18Z (data/estimates/XEL.json): revenue FY2026 $15,606.4M (13 estimates), FY2027 $17,150.1M (14); 15,606.4/14,669 - 1 = 6.39%; 17,150.1/15,606.4 - 1 = 9.89%. The model rows round to 6.35% / 9.9% (within $6M of consensus; DCF +$0.04 on exact consensus, immaterial). Revenue includes pass-through fuel; it does not drive earnings in this set (EPS comes from the rate-base build).
Follows base rate-base growth of $77B->$86B->$90B->$94B (2027-2030, +12%/+5%/+4%) plus ~3% sales growth guide; revenue grows slower than rate base because fuel pass-through is flat.

EBIT here = GAAP operating income + AFUDC-equity and other income (TTM: op income 2,789 (F6) + other ~855 = pretax 2,002 (F81) + interest 1,642 (F67) - 2,789 -> ~3.65B, 23-24% of revenue). Set each year so the rate-base EPS build is matched: EBIT = NI_build / (1 - tax) + interest net of AFUDC-debt. FY2027: 2,893 / 1.08 + 1,750 = 4,429 / 17,150 = 25.8%; FY2028: 3,376 / 1.05 + 2,080 = 5,295 / 18,522 = 28.6%. FY2029-30 hold NOPAT at ~6.7% of avg rate base (0.545 x 8.6% ROE + 0.455 x 4.6% embedded debt cost = 6.78%, rounded down for holdco drag): FY2030 92B x 6.7% = 6.16B / 0.95 = 6.49B / 20.6B = 31.5%.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: XEL's 2026-28 EPS growth (~9-10%) is above the peer median (~8%), which alone would argue for a premium, so I do not widen the discount. It persists because of things that last past the horizon: (a) open wildfire tails - Smokehouse Creek $460M estimated losses with only ~$80M of the $525M policy left and Texas AG penalties not estimable (Q2 release), Marshall ~$640M settlement, and no Colorado liability shield (the 2025 attempt, HB25-1302, dropped the utility-liability trade after utilities balked: KUNC); (b) regulatory lag that the 2026 filings made more durable: PSCo earns 7.22% vs 9.3% allowed and the CPUC imposed a 13-month historical test year; NSPM proposes a 2027-28 base-rate freeze; (c) the $7B equity plan. Round 1 I rounded the relative down to 16.9x with no evidence for the extra 0.3 turn; I now hold the observed 0.91x (17.2x). Before the Smokehouse fire XEL traded at a premium (10-yr ~19.5x); a re-rating to the median is the bull case, not the base.

thesis_break_reason: $63 is ~13.0x my horizon NTM EPS ($4.85) and ~14.1x today's NTM consensus ($4.46), below every regulated peer except ES and ~8% under the $68.72 52-week low, which XEL hit at the 5.3% 10Y peak in late September. Rates alone did not get it there, and the SpaceX base rate shows IPO flows did not either, so a trade below $63 most likely means a fundamental break: a new wildfire liability beyond the ~$80M of remaining Smokehouse cover, a Texas AG outcome that blocks recovery, an ROE cut or rejected NSPM plan / Google ESA, or a downgrade that forces block equity. Re-underwrite rather than average down.

reverse_dcf_check: Engine reverse DCF: the P/E leg ($83.30) needs a 5.8% WACC on my cash flows with a 3.5% Gordon (vs 6.4% used), i.e. a cost of equity ~6.6% at 56/44 weights, about 1.5pt over the 10Y. As a growth-perpetuity check, P/E = (1 - g/ROE)/(k - g): 17.2x fits k ~7.0% with ~3.5% perpetual growth at a 9% earned ROE, or k ~7.7% (my CAPM) only with ~5.3% perpetual growth, which is too much once the post-2040 stranded-cost tail and ROE pressure are counted. So the horizon multiple rests on the market keeping a below-CAPM implied cost of equity for regulated utilities (it has for decades: the group's trailing P/E is at the 78th percentile since 1979, Siblis) and on some of the lag closing. That is rate-sensitive, which is why the bear case is a rates-and-regulation case. Post-horizon risks (wildfire with no CO shield, data-centre shortfall, ROE pressure, stranded-cost tail) are priced by holding the ~9% discount to the peer median, the 3.5% terminal growth and the -$80M adjustment.

reasoning: Round 2. Base rates first: XEL's 12-month price returns 2005-2026 (250 overlapping windows, Twelve Data) had median +8.3%, s.d. 12.6%, 26% negative, 10% below -10%, built mostly in a falling-rate era; now the 10Y is 5.12%, the Fed hiked on 9/16 and Polymarket prices another hike (Dec +25bp 77.5%; 10Y >= 5.5% before 2027 25%). Supervisor findings I accepted: horizon shares 650M was below the 651.9M floor (only the 27.3M 2025 forwards settle before the horizon; 10-Q) -> 658M; NEE dropped, ES back in (median 18.85x unchanged); the NSPM 2027-28 freeze filing and CPUC 13-month historical test year (both 8-Ks, re-read) -> 2027/2028 EPS $4.45/$4.95 (from $4.55/$5.06), NTM $4.85 (from $4.95); my 7.0% WACC + 14x exit was inconsistent -> Gordon 3.5% on a steady-state FY2030 at one WACC. Where I keep my own view: 2028 EPS sits ~1.6% above the strict 9% path ($4.87) because XEL has met guidance 21 years running, the guide is '9%+' and roll-forwards usually add capex; net debt $50.2B (vs $48.5B) because I keep $1.0B of 2027 incremental capex and TTM CFO after dividends is only $3.4B. WACC: I measured XEL's 2-year weekly beta to SPY at 0.21 (Blume 0.47) and moved the cost of equity from 8.4% to 7.7%, WACC 6.4% (supervisor 6.0%). Once the DCF is consistent it says the business is worth about book (~$45/share) at a CAPM cost of capital; the market pays ~2x book on a lower implied cost of equity (reverse DCF 5.8%). Blend: 0.8 x $83.30 + 0.2 x $44.92 = $75.62 fair value (from $79.11), with the P/E leg essentially unchanged ($83.66 -> $83.30: lower EPS, higher 17.2x multiple once I dropped an unsupported round-down). Ladder: I do not centre on the engine median ($75.2): over 12 months prices follow the forward P/E (playbook, Liu-Nissim-Thomas) and the P/E leg sits on the +8% base rate, while the book-value DCF is an anchor the market has not converged to. So the ladder is ~50/50 the engine's scenario mix (bear $63.05 / base $75.62 / bull $86.57, 25/50/25, 11% within-scenario vol) and a P/E-led lognormal (median $82, 16.5% vol), with a fatter left tail for wildfire jump risk (Feb-2024 single-day -8%): median ~$77.5, P(>= $69) 0.76, P(>= $92) 0.15. Kilian's question (does the Anthropic IPO drain liquidity from XEL, and is a dip a buy?): the nearest base rate is the SpaceX IPO, week of 9 June 2026: selling hit the Magnificent Seven (all fell; Moneyfarm) while XEL (+0.2%) and XLU (+0.4%) rose that week and +1.6%/+2.2% through June (Twelve Data). The IPO literature's asset-supply channel (Packer and Spiegel, BIS WP 888) hurts stocks that co-move with the new issue; XEL's correlation to SPY is 0.16 and its holders are income/utility funds. So I expect no meaningful drain on XEL; if one comes through a broad risk-off or a lock-up wave, with the 10Y and fundamentals unchanged, below ~$70 (14.4x my horizon NTM EPS, under the late-September washout of 15.4x NTM) is a buying opportunity; below the $63 thesis break, re-underwrite instead. The bigger near-term drivers are the 10Y and the Oct-29 capital/equity plan. On the WSJ S-1: ~$450B of mostly noncancelable cloud commitments (Google $111B plus a >$160B TPU lease) is a general demand positive through Google, Xcel's largest data-centre counterparty (Pine Island ESA; Abernathy backstop). No named source ties Anthropic load to an Xcel site: Abernathy (SPS) is a Fluidstack campus with a Google backstop and power 100% passed through (TeraWulf 8-K); Anthropic's reported Texas sites are in Central Texas. The S-1's 'more organized and coordinated' opposition risk is already visible in XEL's states (MN AG on the Google ESA, NSPM freeze, CPUC test year). AI-tenant counterparty risk falls first on tariff terms (MN 15-year minimum and exit fees; CO proposed 80% minimum bill and deposits); SPS TX/NM tariffs are not yet filed, which is the gap where shareholders carry it. Research limited to public pages; X/Twitter not used.

model_inputs.dcf_check: Engine DCF $44.92/share vs P/E leg $83.30 (-46%). This is now a consistent build (Gordon 3.5% on a steady-state FY2030 at the same 6.4% WACC, margins that earn ~6.7% after tax on rate base), so the gap is economic, not a modelling error: with the earned return on rate base (~6.7%) barely above a CAPM WACC (6.4%), the regulated asset base is worth about its book value, and the DCF lands at ~1.0x horizon book equity (24.1B now (F88) + ~1.9B retained + ~2.0B forward equity = ~$28B / 658M = ~$43). The market prices the group at ~2x book (XEL now 76.68 / (24,057 / 624.6 = $38.5) = 2.0x) because it capitalises allowed ROEs (9.3-9.6%) at a lower implied cost of equity; the engine's reverse DCF says the P/E leg needs a 5.8% WACC (CoE ~6.6%). The DCF is very sensitive to that spread (6.0% WACC -> $67; 7.0% -> $21; g 3.0% -> $26). I keep its 0.2 weight (P/E-band rule) as the 'no ROE-over-COE premium' anchor; it pulls the blend $7.7 below the P/E leg. dcf_check: Engine DCF $44.92/share vs P/E leg $83.30 (-46%). This is now a consistent build (Gordon 3.5% on a steady-state FY2030 at the same 6.4% WACC, margins that earn ~6.7% after tax on rate base), so the gap is economic, not a modelling error: with the earned return on rate base (~6.7%) barely above a CAPM WACC (6.4%), the regulated asset base is worth about its book value, and the DCF lands at ~1.0x horizon book equity (24.1B now (F88) + ~1.9B retained + ~2.0B forward equity = ~$28B / 658M = ~$43). The market prices the group at ~2x book (XEL now 76.68 / (24,057 / 624.6 = $38.5) = 2.0x) because it capitalises allowed ROEs (9.3-9.6%) at a lower implied cost of equity; the engine's reverse DCF says the P/E leg needs a 5.8% WACC (CoE ~6.6%). The DCF is very sensitive to that spread (6.0% WACC -> $67; 7.0% -> $21; g 3.0% -> $26). I keep its 0.2 weight (P/E-band rule) as the 'no ROE-over-COE premium' anchor; it pulls the blend $7.7 below the P/E leg.
